findings.claim: He calls Claudio and Don Pedro 'two of Don John's most villainous enemies' who were 'close by' and 'saw afar off in the orchard this amiable encounter.'
findings.truth: Borachio says no such thing. The phrases 'two of Don John's most villainous enemies' and 'close by' do not appear anywhere in the play. Borachio says the Prince and Claudio were 'planted and placed and possessed by my master Don John' and 'saw afar off in the orchard this amiable encounter' - the opposite of 'close by'.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg much-ado.txt lines 2512-2517 (Act 3 Scene 1... Act 3 Scene 3, Borachio to Conrade); 'villainous' returns no match near this speech.

findings.claim: They initially try to deny their love again ('I love you with so much of my heart that none is left to protest')
findings.truth: That line is Beatrice's declaration of love in Act 4 Scene 1, moments before 'Kill Claudio'. It is a confession, not a denial, and it is not in the final scene. In Act 5 Scene 4 Benedick says 'by this light, I take thee for pity' and Beatrice 'I yield upon great persuasion'.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg much-ado.txt line 3340 (Act 4 Scene 1) for the misplaced line; lines 4572-4579 (Act 5 Scene 4) for the real denials.

findings.claim: When Beatrice says 'I would my horse had the speed of your tongue,' Benedick replies 'I would my horse had the speed of your departure.'
findings.truth: The speakers are swapped and the reply is invented. Benedick is the one who says 'I would my horse had the speed of your tongue, and so good a continuer.' No line 'I would my horse had the speed of your departure' exists in the play. Beatrice's preceding line is 'A bird of my tongue is better than a beast of yours.'
findings.evidence: Gutenberg much-ado.txt lines 351-356 (Act 1 Scene 1); 'speed of your' returns one match only.

findings.claim: He then sings a song of mourning.
findings.truth: Claudio does not sing. He reads the epitaph from a scroll, hangs it on the tomb, then orders the hymn: 'Now, music, sound, and sing your solemn hymn.' The song is sung by the attendants.

findings.claim: the gulling scene shows she has been hurt before ('he lent [his heart] me awhile')
findings.truth: That line is Beatrice to Don Pedro in Act 2 Scene 1, not the gulling scene (Act 3 Scene 1). Beatrice says nothing of the kind while she is being gulled.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg much-ado.txt line 1221 (Act 2 Scene 1 runs lines 788-1382).

findings.claim: 'If I see any thing tonight why I should not marry her, tomorrow in the congregation, where I should wed, there will I shame her.'
findings.truth: The comma is in the wrong place, which moves 'tomorrow' from the marriage to the shaming. The line reads 'If I see anything tonight why I should not marry her tomorrow, in the congregation, where I should wed, there will I shame her.' The flashcard's 'Tomorrow in the congregation...' repeats the same slip.

findings.claim: What does Beatrice's shift from prose into blank verse signal? / knowledge check option 'Blank verse, signalling emotional sincerity'
findings.truth: Beatrice's soliloquy at the end of Act 3 Scene 1 is rhymed verse, not blank verse: true/adieu, much/such, thee/incite thee, hand/band, I/reportingly. Calling it blank verse is a form error a student would repeat in an analysis answer. 'Verse' is accurate.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg much-ado.txt lines 4042-4053 area (Act 3 Scene 1, 'What fire is in mine ears?' speech).

findings.claim: time management: 5 minutes planning (annotate extract or plan paragraphs), 35 minutes writing (4-5 paragraphs integrating AO1-AO3), 5 minutes checking SPaG (AO4)
findings.truth: That is 45 minutes for a 40-mark answer. The paper carrying this play runs for 2 hours and 80 marks, split evenly between two sections, so about 60 minutes belongs to the Shakespeare answer. The advice under-uses a quarter of the time.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/english-literature-J352.md: 'closed text, 2 hour examination worth 80 marks: 40 marks for Section A and 40 marks for Section B'.

findings.claim: The spec code 'OCR J352' appears in 16 lesson fields, twice with a component code ('Component 02, Section B').
findings.truth: The house validator rejects a unit containing a spec code or a component code. The exam references are factually right, so only the wording changes: name the section, not the code.

findings.claim: Four sentences end on a bare AO code: 'demonstrates AO2.' (L6 exam tip and L7 key fact), 'is strong AO2.' (L7 exam tip) and 'Compare couples for structural AO2.' (L8 practice mark scheme).
findings.truth: The house validator reads an AO code followed immediately by a full stop as a spec-code pattern and rejects the unit. One word added after each code keeps the meaning.

findings.claim: Half the practice questions are labelled '4 marks — Quote Analysis' but carry a 'Top band (7–8)' ladder, and every ladder ends 'Level 5-1' or 'Level 3-1: Descending detail.'
findings.truth: The Shakespeare section sets ONE extended response worth 40 marks, from a choice of two. There is no 4-mark or 8-mark question on the play, and the label and ladder contradict each other. 'Level 1'-'Level 9' band names are also banned house-wide. All 48 questions relabelled to 40 marks and rescaled to the five house bands (33–40 / 25–32 / 17–24 / 9–16 / 1–8).
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/english-literature-J352.md Section B: 'Learners respond to one extended response-style question on their studied play, from a choice of two'; 40 marks for Section B.

findings.claim: Language, structure, and stagecraft in Much Ado: prose vs verse, wit, eavesdropping, and dramatic techniques.
findings.truth: 109 characters. The house validator rejects a lesson description of 100 characters or more, so the unit would fail on load. Shortened without losing a claim.

findings.claim: Benedick says: 'Peace! I will stop your mouth' — and kisses her.
findings.truth: Checked against the trouble-spot list. The primary text gives the line to Benedick with the direction '[Kisses her.]', which is the standard modern attribution. The First Folio gives it to Leonato, but no edit is needed.

summary: Three fabricated or misattributed quotations (Borachio's confession, Beatrice's Act 4 love declaration moved to the final scene, and a swapped-speaker wit exchange with an invented reply), plus a wrong tomb-scene action, a wrong scene reference, a blank-verse mislabel, a 45-minute timing plan for an hour-long answer, 16 banned spec codes and 48 practice ladders that matched no real question.
